newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu welcomes Syrian calming statement.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu welcomes Syrian calming statement.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday welcomed Syria's declaration it had no intentions of starting a war with the Jewish state.

"The prime minister said that he heard the words of the Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara that Syria is not interested in war and said that it was an important and welcome declaration," a statement issued by Netanyahu's office said.

"The prime minister said again that Israel has no aggressive intentions toward Syria and that Israel is interested in convening quickly serious negotiations with Syria to reach a peace agreement with it."
Shara said on Tuesday that Syria was not preparing for an attack on Israel.
"Allegations...that Syria is escalating the situation and massing troops to launch a surprise attack are baseless," Shara said.

"Such allegations coming from the Israeli government are aimed at evading the peace process and the basis on which it was built," he told reporters at Damascus airport while seeing off his Russian counterpart Yevgeny Primakov.
In September, Syria redeployed some 12,000 troops in Lebanon, moving some to within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights, spurring war jitters in Israel.
Israeli security sources said this week that Israel's defence chiefs have told Netanyahu the army needed more than $1 billion because of an increased chance of war with Syria.

Syria has held sporadic bilateral peace talks with Israel since 1991, but no negotiations have been held since Netanyahu took office in June. Syria wants Israel to return the Golan Heights, captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
